//: Story Phase 4, chapter 16: Life Around the Center. Day 2 morning (the bell protocol on the foremast by the bell, then Gristle in the washroom: the door off the Crew Quarters at (3,3), the air scuttle on deck at (6,33)), noon (the galley stove; the stovepipe damper on deck at (12,27); biscuits in the Cargo Hold at (16,4)), evening (the sleeping quarters; the crew camp on the forward deck), 3 AM (three bells; Squawks sleeps at the foot of the captain's bed (13,4)), day 3 morning (the Center on the quarterdeck; the helm at (9,6)).

p4c2.begin.narrate: Overnight, the crew have organised themselves. Nobody asked them to. Nobody had to.

p4c2.protocol_intro: hale: Morning, Captain. We've had a meeting. About the bell.
hale: It's no good for the hours any more, what with the cough. But it's LOUD. So.
hale[resigned]: Quill wrote it up proper. It's on the foremast. Read it before anyone rings anything, please.

p4c2.protocol_intro.tutorial: Read the bell protocol, nailed to the foremast by the ship's bell. (Every alarm also shows on screen: the number of bells, what they mean and where.)
p4c2.protocol_intro.title: Life Around the Center

p4c2.protocol.caption: Nailed to the foremast, in Quill's neat hand.

p4c2.protocol: hale[resigned]: Quill's idea. I said it was unprofessional. He said so is the Center.
hale[concerned]: ...That's one. Outer cloud. Forward, below.

p4c2.protocol.text: GRISTLE! GET OUT OF THERE, IT'S COMING THROUGH THE VENT!

p4c2.protocol: hale[alarmed]: Three. Three's the Center. The WASHROOM.
pete[alarmed]: Captain! It came in through the vent! And Gristle's IN there! I told him! I told him to run!
pete[worried]: The door's stuck. Come and see!

p4c2.protocol.tutorial: The Dead Center has moved into the washroom with Gristle inside. Go below to the Crew Quarters (forward hatch).
p4c2.protocol.title: Washroom Problem

p4c2.washroom_door: Pete is hammering on the washroom door with both fists. A thin yellow light is showing round its edges.

p4c2.washroom_door.text: It won't OPEN! Something's leaning on it!

p4c2.washroom_door: pete[worried]: That's the Center, Gristle. It does that. It leans.
pete[sad]: ...No. There's no other way out. It's a washroom.
A voice is coming through the wall. Muffled, cheerful, and entirely too close.

p4c2.washroom_door.say: garrick[businesslike]: Grand Stenchmaster speaking! Don't panic, Mister Gristle. THE FORECAST SAYS FIFTEEN MINUTES!
p4c2.washroom_door.name: Garrick (through the wall)

p4c2.washroom_door.say: gristle[annoyed]: FIFTEEN MINUTES? You want me to hold my breath for FIFTEEN MINUTES?
p4c2.washroom_door.name: Gristle (in the washroom)

p4c2.washroom_door: captain: Where is he? Where's his voice coming from?
pete: The air scuttle, Captain. On deck, near the bell. It goes straight down into the washroom vent.
pete[tired]: He's shouting advice down it. He does that.
captain[determined]: Then that's our other way out.

p4c2.washroom_door.tutorial: Find the air scuttle on deck (forward, left of the forward hatch) and get Gristle out through it.
p4c2.washroom_door.title: Washroom Problem

p4c2.scuttle: A square grating in the deck, about the size of a large cushion. A thin yellow haze is leaking up out of it.
garrick[businesslike]: Ah, Captain. Consulting with Mister Gristle. Morale is very important in these situations.
You heave the grating up and throw it aside.
It is a very small hole, and Gristle is not a very small man.
There is a lot of grunting. There is some language. There is a noise like a cork leaving a bottle.
Gristle lands on the deck in a heap, coughing, with a toothbrush still in his mouth.
garrick[proud]: Twelve minutes! Three ahead of forecast. You're welcome.
garrick[businesslike]: Well, you're out, aren't you?
gristle[annoyed]: I'm going to think VERY positively about throwing you overboard.
captain[tired]: Somebody put the grating back on.
p4c2.galley_begin: jim[angry]: It's on my STOVE. It's sitting on my STEW!
jim[angry]: It came through the wall, it went round the pots, and it SAT DOWN on my stove like it owns the place!
garrick[businesslike]: Mister Jim. Quick question. Is lunch ready?
jim[angry]: I will put YOU in the stew.
Rook and Sully get an arm each. It takes both of them.
Something below is starting to smell burnt. On this ship, that is an achievement.
jim[sad]: That's my stew. That's my stew burning. And I can't get NEAR it.
garrick[businesslike]: A little burning might add flavour.
jim[angry]: This ship has ENOUGH FLAVOUR!
captain: Can we put the fire out from up here?
jim[concerned]: ...The damper. On the stovepipe, up here on deck. Shut that, and the fire chokes.

p4c2.galley_begin.tutorial: Smother the galley stove: close the damper on the stovepipe (on deck, forward of the main hatch, on the right).
p4c2.galley_begin.title: Galley Problem

p4c2.damper: The stovepipe from the galley comes up through the deck here, smoking busily. There is a damper handle halfway up.
The smoke thins, and stops. Below, something sizzles, sulks, and goes out.
jim[sad]: ...There goes lunch. The stew, the bread, the pudding. It's all in the Center now.
captain: What's left that ISN'T in the Center?
jim: Biscuit. Ship's biscuit, in the crate in the hold. Nobody likes the biscuit.

p4c2.damper.tutorial: Salvage lunch: fetch the biscuit crate from the Cargo Hold (through the galley and down the stairs, keeping clear of the stove), then bring it to Jim.
p4c2.damper.title: Galley Problem

p4c2.biscuits: A crate of ship's biscuit, hard as the planks and very slightly more flavourful.
It has been down here, near the treasure room, for a week. The biscuits have gone faintly yellow round the edges.
You heave the crate onto your shoulder.

p4c2.biscuits.tutorial: Take the biscuits up to Jim, on deck.
p4c2.biscuits.title: Galley Problem

p4c2.lunch_served: You set the crate down in front of Jim.
garrick[delighted]: Oh, they've gone yellow at the edges. That'll be the Center. Adds a certain something.
jim[angry]: Say 'flavour'. Go on. I dare you.
The crew eat their biscuits in silence, sitting on the deck, looking at the stovepipe.
p4c2.quarters_begin: The crew came up the forward hatch in a hurry an hour ago, carrying everything they sleep on: pillows, blankets, a hammock or two, and one rolled-up rug that nobody will admit to owning.
hale[resigned]: It's in the sleeping quarters, Captain. Garrick's board says it'll sit there till morning.
hale: So we're sleeping on deck.

p4c2.quarters_begin.tutorial: See the crew bedded down on the forward deck. (Talk to Barnacle Bob at the camp.)
p4c2.quarters_begin.title: Sleeping Quarters

p4c2.camp: bob[sad]: Nobody's slept properly in a week, Captain. Not one of us.
bob[sad]: Wick sleeps with his head in a bucket now. Finch sleeps standing up, like a horse. I've been sleeping in the rigging when I can get up there.
pete[tired]: At least we've got our pillows.
It is yellow. Not stained yellow. Not yellowish. Yellow, all the way through, the colour of old mustard.
bob[surprised]: That's never your pillow. What's it smell like?
Pete snatches it away and hugs it to his chest.
pete[queasy]: I did it once. Just once. I'm still doing it now, in a way.
captain: Get some sleep, all of you. That's an order.
p4c2.night_wake: You are asleep. You are dreaming about merchant ships. Fat ones, low in the water, with gold in the hold and no parrots on them at all.

p4c2.night_wake.tutorial: Three bells in the night: the Center is crossing the deck where the crew are sleeping. Get Squawks first (at the foot of your bed), then get out there.
p4c2.night_wake.title: Night Evacuation

p4c2.night_squawks: captain[tender]: Bad bells. Up you come.
You scoop him up, blanket, cap and all, and tuck him inside your coat. He doesn't complain. He's done this before.

p4c2.night_squawks.tutorial: Out on deck, and get everyone aft!
p4c2.night_squawks.title: Night Evacuation

p4c2.night_deck: Out on deck it's black as tar, except for the forward hatch, where a thick yellow glow is spilling up out of the sleeping quarters and rolling aft over the camp.
pete[alarmed]: I've got it! Captain, I saved it! I grabbed the first thing I—
He looks down at what he's carrying. It's a jug of Frog Grog.
Below the rail the black water boils. Something big thrashes in the dark. Then something else. Then a great many somethings.
captain[concerned]: They liked it a lot.
The Grand Stenchmaster gallops out of the dark with three pillows under one arm, a frying pan under the other, and a small, heavy, clinking bag held in his teeth.
He spits the bag into his hand.
captain[angry]: GARRICK. Did you just rescue your MONEY before your crewmates?
garrick[proud]: Pillows for comfort. Pan for breakfast. Coins for continuity of office!
garrick[surprised]: The crew can run! Coins can't run!
From the quarterdeck, the whole crew watch the yellow glow settle over their blankets like a cat on a warm chair.
p4c2.quarterdeck_begin: It comes up over the stern rail this time, slow and yellow, and settles over the quarterdeck. Over the helm. Over the wheel.
nell[alarmed]: Captain! I had to leave the wheel! I can't get back to it!
nell[concerned]: She's falling off already. Nobody on the helm, she'll swing round into the wind.
garrick[businesslike]: It'll move shortly, Captain. I predicted it hours ago. It's all on the board.
garrick[proud]: A circular arrow. The Center goes round.
garrick[businesslike]: Ah. That's an atmospheric sausage.
You look at the map. You look at Garrick. You look at the long drop over the rail into the sea, and at the several hundred feet of rope within easy reach.
captain[resigned]: I'm going to walk away now, Garrick. Before I do something the Admiralty would call legally questionable.
nell[alarmed]: It's moving off, Captain! The wheel's clear!

p4c2.quarterdeck_begin.tutorial: The quarterdeck is clear. Take the wheel (up the stairs, at the stern) and bring her back on course.
p4c2.quarterdeck_begin.title: Quarterdeck Blocked

p4c2.helm: The wheel is still warm, and faintly sticky. You don't think about why.
The Queen Anne's Revenge swings, slowly and grumpily, back onto her heading.
nell[happy]: On course, Captain. South-sou'west. Only lost us half a morning.
captain[tired]: Half a morning. On a good day, that's half a merchant ship.
